title: Stage-gate: procurement stagegate and privileged key review
next_steps: Redwood to send redlined MSA + DPA examples
SE to run small connectivity preflight with Atlas staging VPC
Security intake: provide SOC2 summary & KMS architecture deck
action_items: Ethan Brooks: Share pricing band and committed throughput tiers (due: 2025-10-01)
Maya Singh: Run VPC peering preflight checklist and share results (due: 2025-10-03)
Luis Ortega / Sofia Park: Provide list of required DPA clauses and data residency constraints (due: 2025-10-06)
summary: Procurement stage-gate with procurement, security and platform to validate MSA/DPA exceptions, KMS keying, and SLAs before exec approval. Main concerns: privileged key custody, egress costs, and guaranteed P50/P95 latency for inference. Redwood AE + SE walked through deployment options and proposed Dedicated + Private control plane with customer KMS integration.
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-09-26 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Ethan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Priya (Atlas Procurement), Luis (Atlas CISO), Daniel (Platform Eng), Sofia (Legal)

[00:00] Ethan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time, we wanted to run through the stage gate items you listed in the intake — procurement, legal, and a quick tech walk. I'm Ethan from Redwood.
[00:22] Priya - Procurement: Hi Ethan, thanks. We're trying to make sure the MSA and DPA language aligns with Atlas's vendor policy, plus we have a privileged keys question — custody of KMS and escrow options.
[00:35] Maya (SE): Hi all, Maya here. I'll cover the KMS integration and connectivity preflight. Quick note, sometimes the product name in notes shows as "Redwood Dedicate" in transcripts, it's Redwood Dedicated.
[00:48] Luis - CISO: Good morning. From security perspective we need to confirm: can you support customer-managed KMS? And do you offer an HSM-backed path for private deployments? Also retention, audit logs, and SSO integration — SAML 2.0 with SCIM — those are must-haves.
[01:15] Ethan (AE): Yes on SAML/SCIM and audit logs. For KMS there are two patterns — customer-managed keys in our Private deployment, or a bring-your-own-key (BYOK) integration with Dedicated with limited key custody. The HSM-backed option is available for Private installs; for hosted we're SOC2 but keys stay with Redwood unless we do a bespoke escrow arrangement.
[01:42] Daniel - Platform Eng: When you say Private, do you mean we run a customer control plane in our VPC, or you host it but isolate network? Latency is critical for our inference path — P95 under 150ms for our 1k qps baseline. Also we need the KV cache behavior for multi-tenant workloads explained.
[02:05] Maya (SE): Private = customer VPC + control plane we hand over, or a managed private control plane that lives in a customer VPC depending on the package. For the latency: Dedicated fixed GPU pools give predictable throughput; the runtime supports prefix KV cache and model variants. I'll schedule a perf readout but a rough baseline: for quantized models we commonly hit P95 < 120ms for token generation for seq length ~512 in Dedicated. Your qps shapes will affect batching.
[02:42] Priya - Procurement: From procurement's lens — we need to understand pricing bands for committed throughput, what triggers overage pricing, and minimum term for reserved capacity. Also DPA exceptions — we can't accept broad subprocessing clauses, need subprocessor list and EU data residency.
[03:05] Ethan (AE): Our committed tiers start at a 6-month minimum for Dedicated reserved capacity; pricing bands are pegged to average tokens and burst capacity. I'll send a banded rate card. On subprocessors we provide a list and can add contractual notification windows for changes per DPA.
[03:28] Sofia - Legal: On the DPA, we typically ask for tighter deletion windows and an audit right for data handling. Does Redwood provide auditable logs of model access and token retention? Also are you able to accept standard indemnity caps?
[03:50] Ethan (AE): We can support audit logs and provide retention settings. Deletion windows depend on deployment mode — Hosted has a default retention, Dedicated and Private can be configured to shorter windows. Indemnity caps are negotiable; we'll flag that with legal.
[04:10] Luis - CISO: Another point: vendor gating requires ISO 27001 or SOC2 Type II evidence. Do you have both? And if we require an on-premish air-gapped deployment, what's the gating timeline?
[04:28] Maya (SE): We have SOC2 Type II and an ISO 27001 program in progress — can provide SOC2 report redacted. Air-gapped/on-prem package exists but is longer lead time — typically 10-14 weeks for packaging, validation, and keying.
[04:47] Priya - Procurement: That timeline is important for our go/no-go. Execs want a procurement decision by mid-October, so if packaging is 10-14 weeks that's too long unless we do a hybrid approach.
[05:02] Ethan (AE): Understood. Hybrid — Dedicated reserved capacity with VPC peering and BYOK may be the fastest path to compliance and lower friction.
[05:15] Daniel - Platform Eng: For BYOK — are we handing over KMS keys to Redwood or do you integrate with our KMS via a connector? We need to know where private keys live and how rotation works.
[05:30] Maya (SE): BYOK integrates with your KMS via a connector — Redwood doesn't store plaintext keys. We use envelope encryption and the runtime only has ephemeral key material for the session. Rotation is orchestrated by you; we support rotation hooks. Sometimes notes show "K V cache" or "K V" spelled out in transcripts but it's KV (key-value) cache.
[05:56] Sofia - Legal: On encryption-at-rest and in-transit — do you support TLS 1.3, and can you provide FIPS 140-2 validated HSM logs if we need that level for keys?
[06:10] Maya (SE): We use TLS 1.3 for in-transit. For FIPS/HSM logs we can do HSM-backed private deployments and provide attestation logs; hosted won't by default have FIPS-level key manifests unless engaged as an enterprise agreement.
[06:30] Priya - Procurement: Pricing: do you have termination for convenience terms? We need reasonable exit assistance and data egress estimates — our legal asks for egress cost caps during the first 30 days of termination.
[06:46] Ethan (AE): We typically offer an exit assistance addendum for enterprise deals which includes data export and a capped egress buffer. I'll surface a template.
[06:55] Daniel - Platform Eng: Can we run a small proof-of-concept with a trimmed down model on Dedicated to validate latency and cost? We're sensitive to model size because of token cost and latency.
[07:10] Ethan (AE): Yes — POC is standard. We'll propose a 4-week pilot on pre-configured Dedicated nodes with a pilot SLA and sample throughput.
[07:20] Priya - Procurement: What's the signing path — procurement needs an MSA, DPA and a SOW for the pilot. If we get MSA redlines early we can route through faster.
[07:34] Sofia - Legal: We'll need to redline the DPA for deletion and cross-border transfer constraints. Also, subprocessor notifications need minimum 30 days.
[07:46] Maya (SE): Noted. We'll produce a template DPA and point to the subprocessors. In practice we support region pinning to prevent cross-border transfer for the data plane.
[08:02] Luis - CISO: A technical ask: can you show how model variants fallback works if a Dedicated pool is saturated? We don't want user-facing errors.
[08:14] Maya (SE): The runtime supports smart routing and fallback to compatible model variants or lower-tier regions. There's an automated fallback policy you can configure — canary/fallbacking, and also an automatic degrade to a smaller context length to preserve throughput. We'll demo this in the SE follow-up.
[08:35] Daniel - Platform Eng: Also curious about metrics — can we get token-level cost breakdowns and per-route tracing? Our platform team wants billed tokens per feature for FinOps.
[08:47] Ethan (AE): Yes Redwood Console exposes token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards and trace hooks. We can add a sample dashboard to the POC SOW.
[09:00] Priya - Procurement: Regarding DPA exceptions — we can't accept open-ended subprocessor clause, and we need an option for data residency within the EU for a portion of the workload. Can you guarantee EU-only processing?
[09:18] Maya (SE): EU-only processing is supported via region pinning in Private and Dedicated — we can pin the inference path to EU datacenters and ensure data doesn't egress. For hosted-tier, we can use dedicated hardware in EU regions under a region-residency commitment.
[09:40] Sofia - Legal: On indemnities — our standard is engineering-level negligence carve-outs, and we'd like mutual indemnities with a cap tied to fees. Is that acceptable?
[09:53] Ethan (AE): We'll take that back to legal, but mutual caps tied to fees are standard negotiation. We'll try to provide precedent language.
[10:05] Priya - Procurement: For procurement timeline, if we get redlines by next week, we can route for approval by Oct 10. Otherwise it slips.
[10:16] Ethan (AE): We'll aim to deliver redlined MSA/DPA templates by Oct 1.
[10:22] Maya (SE): I'll schedule the connectivity preflight next week — VPC peering checklist and minimal firewall rules. Can we get a point of contact for network?
[10:32] Daniel - Platform Eng: That's me. I'll share the staging VPC details and a security group template.
[10:38] Priya - Procurement: One more procurement ask: reseller channels and invoicing — we need to know if Redwood invoices directly or via a partner. Also tax documentation for cross-border invoicing.
[10:50] Ethan (AE): We invoice directly for enterprise contracts; can support partner invoicing in special cases. We'll include billing path options in the follow-up.
[11:00] Luis - CISO: Quick question on pen testing — do you allow customer-led pen tests against Private/Dedicated deployments? What's the process?
[11:12] Maya (SE): Yes, through a scheduled window and an authorization form — we have a pen test playbook and require coordination. We'll share the playbook.
[11:22] Sofia - Legal: Also, please confirm retention windows in writing and sample audit logs for model access. We'll need those attached to the DPA.
[11:30] Ethan (AE): We'll provide the retention spec and a sample audit log.
[11:36] Priya - Procurement: Ok, anything else on SLAs? Our ops team wants an uptime SLA and an SLO for request latency. Are you comfortable with P99 SLOs or only P95?
[11:48] Maya (SE): We publish both P95 and P99 latency profiles; guaranteed SLOs are typically P95 for token generation in standard tiers and P99 can be added into enterprise SLAs with specific capacity reservations. We'll scope that in the SOW.
[12:05] Daniel - Platform Eng: For cost controls, does Redwood support per-route quotas and throttles so we can isolate a single feature's runaway costs?
[12:18] Ethan (AE): Yes — per-route quotas, rate limits and token caps per API key. FinOps can be integrated with console alerts.
[12:30] Priya - Procurement: Great. Let's recap next steps.
[12:35] Ethan (AE): Recap: 1) Redwood to send redlined MSA + DPA templates and subprocessors list by 2025-10-01. 2) SE (Maya) to run VPC peering preflight with Daniel — schedule for next week. 3) Provide SOC2 report and retention/audit log samples. 4) Pricing band + pilot SOW for 4-week Dedicated pilot.
[13:05] Priya - Procurement: That works. One ask — can you add a refundable pilot deposit option if we commit to production afterwards?
[13:15] Ethan (AE): We can propose a deposit creditable to the first committed month in the SOW. I'll include that option.
[13:23] Sofia - Legal: We'll start compiling DPA redlines and circulate to Ethan and Maya.
[13:30] Daniel - Platform Eng: I'll send the staging VPC details to Maya after the call.
[13:36] Ethan (AE): Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts.
[13:40] [END]
notes: SE to demo fallback routing in follow-up technical session
Finance to review pilot deposit crediting in SOW
